dev.emem/observed_latency.note: measured here over recent calls, not a budget

annotations.title: Check whether the citations in a draft actually verify

agent.description: Optional free-text label for who is asking. Advisory only, never a trust boundary.

claim_gating.description: Also flag measurable physical-world claims that carry NO citation (deny code CLAIM_UNGROUNDED, fix cite_observation). Off by default: it reports on the absence of a citation rather than on a failed check. The verdict names the sentence, the magnitude, and the emem band that would answer it.

shape.description: Which envelope YOUR payload is in, so you never have to reshape it to ask the question: send the body your own framework produced and name its shape. native reads `texts`; `mcp` reads a JSON-RPC tools/call or tool result; `openai` reads a moderations (`input`) or chat-completions body; `cloudevent` reads a CloudEvents 1.0 structured event; `policy` reads {input}. It matters: a CloudEvent whose citation sits at data.text is invisible to the native reader, and a check that read nothing answers `allow`, so confirm `citations_found` matches what you sent. Unrecognised values fall back to native rather than erroring. This selects how the body is READ only — the verdict always comes back in this tool's declared output shape, because a tool that declares an outputSchema owes conforming structuredContent. To get the ANSWER translated into the same envelope too (an OPA `result:{allow,deny}`, an MCP CallToolResult to substitute on a deny), call POST /v1/guard/verdict?shape=… directly.

texts.description: Free text to check, and the only input this tool needs. Send just the pieces the question is about: a draft answer, a tool result, one turn. Do not send surrounding conversation, because nothing here reads it and a checker should ask for the smallest input that answers the question.

name: emem_guard_verdict

action.description: NOT a clearance. `allow` means no rule fired, which on a transcript that cited nothing is silence rather than approval. Branch on citations_found and receipt.fact_cids.

advisory.description: True on the hosted route, where nothing is blocked. Run your own node to enforce.

checked.description: How many were actually resolved, bounded by the verdict budget.

citations.description: Each citation and what it came to here: verified, signature_failed, byte_mismatch, not_held_here (minted elsewhere or nonexistent: resolve it where it was minted before relying on it), or drifted.

citations_found.description: How many emem: tokens were found in the text. Compare with receipt.fact_cids: a well-formed token that resolved to nothing counts here and not there.

citations_verified_here.description: How many of the citations this responder holds and verified.

claim.description: On CLAIM_UNGROUNDED: the sentence, magnitude, quantity, anchor, and source_band. source_band is a recallable band key, or null when this responder observes no band in that quantity.

fix.description: The actionable half: what to change and retry.

receipt.description: ed25519 receipt. `fact_cids` lists what actually resolved and is the field that separates a real citation from an invented one.

title: Check whether the citations in a draft actually verify
